[notes-n1] Notes 1. The second-order moment
Unit 7 sorted the columns with λ_{lim}; Unit 8 designed the short ones, for the first-order moments and the imperfection. This Unit designs the slender ones. Nothing from Unit 8 is thrown away: the cover, the charts, the direct check, the bars and the links all stay. Two things are new: the second-order moment, and the second axis.
Second-order effect (EC2 5.8.1) The additional moment caused by the deformation of the structure. In an isolated column, the axial load N_{Ed} acts on the deflected shape, so at the critical section it has a lever arm e_2, the deflection, on top of the first-order eccentricity e_1 (the analysed moment and the imperfection, divided by N_{Ed}).
EQUATION (9.1): M = N_{Ed}\,(e_1 + e_2)
[Figure: The hook: the bow of a slender strip adds to the offset of the load, so the moment grows faster than the load.]
Why “by itself”: the extra moment N_{Ed}e_2 bends the column further, which increases e_2, which increases the moment again. In a column that is strong enough the sequence settles at a larger, finite deflection; near the buckling load it never settles. For a short column the extra moment is small, under about 10% of the first-order moment, and EC2 lets you ignore it: that is what λ ≤ λ_{lim} means (EC2 5.8.2(6), 5.8.3.1).
Three methods (EC2 5.8.5) The general method (5.8.6) follows the non-linear behaviour step by step. Two simplified methods follow: nominal stiffness (5.8.7) reduces the stiffness and magnifies the moment; nominal curvature (5.8.8) assumes a curvature at the critical section and turns it into a deflection. This course uses nominal curvature, as the RDF, the course notes and the RC Design app do. It suits an isolated column with a constant axial force and a known l_0.
Quick check (not graded): A slender column deflects 30 mm at mid-height. N_{Ed} = 1000 kN and the first-order moment there is 50 kN m. The moment at mid-height is about
Options: 50 kN m | 80 kN m | 30 kN m | 1050 kN m
Explanation shown after answering: 50 + 1000 × 0.030 = 80 kN m: the deflection adds 60% here. 50 ignores the second-order moment; 30 is N_{Ed}e_2 alone; 1050 adds a force to a moment.
Key points:
- A slender column carries M = N_{Ed}(e_1 + e_2): the deflection e_2 adds a second-order moment M_2 = N_{Ed}e_2.
- λ ≤ λ_{lim}: M_2 may be ignored (Unit 8). λ > λ_{lim}: add it (this Unit).
- The course method is nominal curvature, EC2 5.8.8.

[notes-n2] Notes 2. Nominal curvature
Nominal curvature does not compute the deflection from a stiffness. It assumes the critical section is close to failure, with both layers of bars about to yield, which fixes a curvature; it corrects that curvature for a high axial load (K_r) and for creep (K_φ); and a sine-shaped deflected shape turns the curvature into a deflection.
[Figure: Nominal curvature: both layers at yield give the basic curvature 1/r_0; a sine-shaped deflection over l_0 gives e_2.]
EQUATION (9.2): \frac{1}{r_0} = \frac{\varepsilon_{yd}}{0.45\,d},\qquad \varepsilon_{yd} = \frac{f_{yd}}{E_s} = \frac{435}{200\,000} = 0.00217
d is the effective depth in the plane of bending: d = h − d_2 for bars on two opposite faces (EC2 5.8.8.3(2)). The strain changes by 2ε_{yd} over about 0.9d, hence 0.45d.
EQUATION (9.3): K_r = \frac{n_u - n}{n_u - n_{bal}} \le 1,\qquad n = \frac{N_{Ed}}{A_c f_{cd}},\quad n_u = 1 + \omega,\quad \omega = \frac{A_s f_{yd}}{A_c f_{cd}},\quad n_{bal} = 0.4
K_r: the axial-load correction (EC2 5.8.8.3(3)) A heavily loaded column crushes before its tension bars yield, so its curvature at failure is smaller: K_r falls as n rises. ω here is A_sf_{yd}/(A_cf_{cd}), not the chart’s A_sf_{yk}/(bhf_{ck}). K_r needs the steel, which needs K_r: start with K_r = 1 and iterate (§4).
EQUATION (9.4): K_\varphi = 1 + \beta\,\varphi_{ef} \ge 1,\qquad \beta = 0.35 + \frac{f_{ck}}{200} - \frac{\lambda}{150},\qquad \varphi_{ef} = \varphi(\infty,t_0)\,\frac{M_{0Eqp}}{M_{0Ed}}
K_φ: creep (EC2 5.8.8.3(4), 5.8.4) Creep lets the column keep deflecting under the long-term part of its load. φ(∞,t_0) comes from EC2 Figure 3.1 or Annex B; the course and the app use Annex B with RH 80% (outside), t_0 = 30 days, cement class R and h_0 = 2A_c/u. M_{0Eqp}/M_{0Ed} is the quasi-permanent share of the first-order moment: 0.67 unless the analysis gives it. φ_{ef} may be taken as 0 if φ(∞,t_0) ≤ 2, λ ≤ 75 and M_{0Ed}/N_{Ed} ≥ h (EC2 5.8.4(4)).
EQUATION (9.5): \frac{1}{r} = K_r K_\varphi\,\frac{1}{r_0},\qquad e_2 = \frac{1}{r}\,\frac{l_0^2}{c},\ c = 10\ (\approx\pi^2),\qquad M_2 = N_{Ed}\,e_2
Worked Example 9.1, about z: 300 × 300, d = 254 mm, l_0 = 5.0 m, λ = 57.7, N_{Ed} = 1000 kN, C30/37. 1/r_0 = 0.002175/(0.45 × 254) = 1.903 × 10⁻⁵ per mm. Annex B with h_0 = 2 × 90 000/1200 = 150 mm gives φ(∞,t_0) = 1.71, so φ_{ef} = 1.71 × 0.67 = 1.143; β = 0.35 + 0.15 − 57.7/150 = 0.115 and K_φ = 1.132. With K_r = 1: e_2 = 1.132 × 1.903 × 10⁻⁵ × 5000²/10 = 53.8 mm and M_2 = 53.8 kN m. The iteration of §4 settles at K_r = 0.724: e_2 = 39.0 mm, M_2 = 39.0 kN m.
Quick check (not graded): A column bent about its minor axis has d = 204 mm and B500 bars. Its basic curvature 1/r_0 is
Options: 1.90 × 10⁻⁵ /mm | 2.37 × 10⁻⁵ /mm | 4.74 × 10⁻⁵ /mm | 1.07 × 10⁻⁵ /mm
Explanation shown after answering: 0.002175/(0.45 × 204) = 2.37 × 10⁻⁵ per mm. A shallower section bends more for the same bar strains. 1.90 × 10⁻⁵ is for d = 254 mm; 4.74 × 10⁻⁵ doubles it; 1.07 × 10⁻⁵ uses 0.002175/d.
Key points:
- 1/r_0 = ε_{yd}/(0.45d); 1/r = K_rK_φ/r_0; e_2 = (1/r)l_0²/10; M_2 = N_{Ed}e_2.
- K_r ≤ 1 falls with axial load and needs the steel; K_φ ≥ 1 grows with creep.
- ω in K_r is A_sf_{yd}/(A_cf_{cd}), not the chart’s ω.

[notes-n3] Notes 3. Design moments: braced and unbraced
The imperfection is part of the first-order moment, as in Unit 8. For the four candidates the course takes it as the RC Design app does (its decision D16): at the ends it is added to both magnitudes; in the equivalent moment it is added once, in the direction of M_{02}.
EQUATION (9.6): M_{02} = |M|_{max} + N_{Ed}e_i,\quad M_{01} = |M|_{min} + N_{Ed}e_i,\qquad M_{0e} = 0.6|M|_{max} \pm 0.4|M|_{min} + N_{Ed}e_i \ \ge\ 0.4M_{02}
The minus sign is for double curvature, where the end moments have opposite signs. RDF §14 and Column3.xlsx add e_i to both magnitudes inside M_{0e} too, which in double curvature lowers M_{0e}; the app takes the larger reading. In this Unit’s examples the governing candidate is the same either way.
EQUATION (9.7): \text{braced:}\quad M_{Ed} = \max\left(M_{02},\; M_{0e} + M_2,\; M_{01} + 0.5M_2,\; N_{Ed}e_0\right)
EQUATION (9.8): \text{unbraced:}\quad M_{Ed} = \max\left(M_{02} + M_2,\; N_{Ed}e_0\right)
[Figure: Where the moments add. A braced end does not move, so M_2 is zero there and peaks near mid-height, where the first-order moment is smaller. In an unbraced column the end itself moves, and M_2 adds at the end.]
M_{0e} + M_2 checks the section near mid-height. M_{02} checks the end. M_{01} + 0.5M_2 comes from BS 8110 (3.8.3.2) through the RDF and can govern in double curvature when M_2 is large. Activity 9A found all four branches; the table gives the results (kN m).

Key points:
- Braced: M_{Ed} = max(M_{02}, M_{0e} + M_2, M_{01} + 0.5M_2, N_{Ed}e_0); unbraced: max(M_{02} + M_2, N_{Ed}e_0).
- M_{0e} = 0.6|M|_{max} ± 0.4|M|_{min} + N_{Ed}e_i ≥ 0.4M_{02}, minus in double curvature.
- Single curvature with a large M_2: mid-height governs. Double curvature with a small M_2: the end governs.

[notes-n4] Notes 4. The K_r loop and the bars
K_r depends on the steel, and the steel on the design moment, which depends on K_r. The loop: take K_r = 1, find M_2 and M_{Ed}, design A_s (chart or Lab), compute ω and a new K_r, and repeat until K_r stops changing. Two to four passes are enough; K_r = 1 alone is safe but wasteful. Worked Example 9.1 about z (n = 0.654):

Then come the bars provided, and a final check: with more steel than required, K_r rises a little, so M_2 is recomputed with the bars provided (K′_r, M′_{Ed}) and checked against M_{Rd}. For Worked Example 9.1, 4H20 = 1257 mm²: ω = 1257 × 435/(90 000 × 17.0) = 0.357, K′_r = (1.357 − 0.654)/(1.357 − 0.4) = 0.735, M′_2 = 39.6 and M′_{Ed} = 92.1 kN m ≤ M_{Rd} = 96.5 kN m.

Options: nothing: more steel only helps | K_r rises a little: recompute M_2 and check M′_{Ed} ≤ M_{Rd} | take K_r = 1 for the bars provided | the column becomes short
Explanation shown after answering: More steel raises n_u = 1 + ω and so K_r (0.735 here), and M_2 with it. The section gains more than M_2 does, so the bars still work, but the check must use M′_{Ed}: 92.1 against 96.5 kN m.
Key points:
- Iterate: K_r = 1 → M_{Ed} → A_s → ω → K_r, until K_r settles (two to four passes).
- With the bars provided, recompute K′_r, M′_2, M′_{Ed} and check M′_{Ed} ≤ M_{Rd}.
- The charts and the chart rule are those of Unit 8.

[notes-n5] Notes 5. Both axes: the screening
A column has two axes, and Unit 7 classified both. About an axis with no analysed moment only the imperfection acts, so r_m = 1, C = 0.7 and λ_{lim} is low, about 10 to 15: that axis is usually slender. Worked Example 8.1 is non-slender about z (λ_{lim} = 38.8) but slender about y (λ_{lim} = 11.5 < 15.6).
Imperfection in one direction (EC2 5.8.9(2)) Design each direction separately as a first step. The imperfection need only be taken in the direction where it is most unfavourable. The course applies this as the app does: two cases, the imperfection (and the floor N_{Ed}e_0) about z with y at its moment without them, then the reverse; the worse case governs. Without its imperfection a slender axis still carries M_2, because nominal curvature does not depend on the first-order moment.
EQUATION (9.9): \frac{\lambda_y}{\lambda_z} \le 2 \ \text{and}\ \frac{\lambda_z}{\lambda_y} \le 2,\qquad \frac{e_y/h}{e_z/b} \le 0.2\ \ \text{or}\ \ \frac{e_z/b}{e_y/h} \le 0.2,\qquad e_y = \frac{M_{Ed,z}}{N_{Ed}},\ e_z = \frac{M_{Ed,y}}{N_{Ed}}
If both conditions hold, one axis dominates and the separate designs are enough (EC2 5.8.9(3)); M_{Ed,z} and M_{Ed,y} include the second-order moments, and for a rectangle h_{eq} = h and b_{eq} = b. If not, the two axes are checked together (§6). Column3.xlsx tests whether the larger ratio exceeds 0.2, which is always true because the two ratios are reciprocals (audit C-15): the test is that one of them is at most 0.2.
[Figure: The screening: near either axis one moment dominates and the axes may be designed separately. C12 of the app passes; Worked Example 9.1 and Faded Example 9.2 do not.]
Quick check (not graded): A 250 × 600 column has λ_y/λ_z = 2.4, and one relative eccentricity is 0.1 times the other. Is a biaxial check needed?
Options: no: 0.1 ≤ 0.2 | yes: λ_y/λ_z > 2 | no: only slender columns need it | only if N_{Ed}/N_{Rd} > 0.1
Explanation shown after answering: Both conditions must hold for separate designs; the slenderness ratios fail (2.4 > 2), so Eq. 5.39 is needed whatever the eccentricities. N_{Ed}/N_{Rd} only sets the exponent a.
Key points:
- An axis with no analysed moment usually is slender (C = 0.7): check it.
- Imperfection in one direction at a time; N_{Ed}e_0 goes with it; M_2 stays on a slender axis.
- Separate designs only if λ_y/λ_z and λ_z/λ_y ≤ 2 and one relative eccentricity ratio ≤ 0.2.

[notes-n6] Notes 6. Biaxial design: estimate and check
When the screening fails, the course works in two moves: an estimate of the bars with the enhanced moment of RDF §14 (the BS 8110 method), then the EC2 check, Eq. 5.39, with the bars provided.
EQUATION (9.10): \frac{M_{Ed,z}}{h'} \ge \frac{M_{Ed,y}}{b'}:\quad M'_z = M_{Ed,z} + \beta\,\frac{h'}{b'}\,M_{Ed,y},\qquad \beta = 1 - \frac{N_{Ed}}{b\,h\,f_{ck}} \ \ge 0.3
h′ and b′ are the effective depths for bending about z and y; if M_{Ed,y}/b′ is the larger, swap the roles. The section is designed about one axis for M′, with the chart or Lab tab 5.
EQUATION (9.11): \left(\frac{M_{Ed,z}}{M_{Rd,z}}\right)^{a} + \left(\frac{M_{Ed,y}}{M_{Rd,y}}\right)^{a} \le 1,\qquad N_{Rd} = A_c f_{cd} + A_s f_{yd}
N_{Ed}/N_{Rd} ≤ 0.1 0.7 ≥ 1.0
a 1.0 1.5 2.0
M_{Rd,z} and M_{Rd,y} are the moment resistances of the bars provided about each axis at N_{Ed}: read μ from the chart at ν and the ω of the bars, or use Lab tab 5. a is interpolated linearly between the values in the table (EC2 5.8.9(4)). Both imperfection cases of §5 are checked; the larger sum governs.

[examples-x3] Example 3 · Explain-type questions
Exam type short written answers Time ≈ 3 min each
Questions
- A slender column’s moment grows by itself. Explain why, and why EC2 lets a short column ignore it.
- Why is M_2 not added to M_{02} in a braced column, when it is in an unbraced one?
- More bars raise the design moment of a slender column. Why, and is adding bars still worth it?
- A column has no analysed moment about y. Why must it still be checked about y, and why can the biaxial check govern?
Write your four answers first, then open the model answers one by one.
## Answer 1 The deflection adds a lever arm
The axial load acts on the deflected column, so at the critical section its eccentricity is e_1 + e_2. The extra moment N_{Ed}e_2 bends the column further, which increases e_2 and the moment again; a strong enough column settles at a larger deflection, a column near its buckling load does not. In a short column e_2 is small and the extra moment stays below about 10% of the first-order moment; EC2 sets λ_{lim} so that columns below it may ignore it (5.8.2(6), 5.8.3.1).
## Answer 2 Where the deflection is
In a braced column the ends cannot move sideways, so the deflection, and M_2, is zero at the ends, where the largest first-order moment M_{02} acts; M_2 peaks near mid-height, where the first-order moment is the smaller M_{0e}. Hence the candidates M_{02}, M_{0e} + M_2 and M_{01} + 0.5M_2. In an unbraced column the end itself sways, so the deflection and M_{02} act at the same section: M_{02} + M_2.
## Answer 3 More steel, more curvature
K_r = (n_u − n)/(n_u − 0.4) with n_u = 1 + ω: more steel raises n_u and so K_r, the nominal curvature and M_2. Physically, a more heavily reinforced section can bend further before it fails. It is still worth it, because M_{Rd} grows faster than M_2: in Worked Example 9.1 the bars provided raise M_{Ed} from 91.5 to 92.1 kN m while M_{Rd} is 96.5 kN m. It is why the final check uses K′_r with the bars provided.
## Answer 4 The unloaded axis
About y the imperfection still acts, and the section must carry at least N_{Ed}e_0. With no end moments r_m = 1 and C = 0.7, so λ_{lim} is low and the column is often slender about y; nominal curvature then adds M_2 whatever the first-order moment. These moments act at the same time as the moment about z. The screening asks whether one axis dominates; when it does not, the combination can need more steel than either axis alone: 4H16 to 4H20 in Faded Example 9.2, 4H20 to 8H20 in Worked Example 9.1.

[glossary-axial-load-ratio-n] Glossary: axial load ratio n
axial load ratio n: N_{Ed} /(A_c f_{cd} ) with f_{cd} = 0.85f_{ck} /1.5: the n of λ_{lim} and of K_r . Not the ν of the charts.

[glossary-basic-curvature-1-r-0] Glossary: basic curvature 1/r_0
basic curvature 1/r_0: ε_{yd} /(0.45d): the curvature with both layers of bars at yield (EC2 5.8.8.3(1)).

[glossary-biaxial-rdf-14] Glossary: β (biaxial, RDF §14)
β (biaxial, RDF §14): 1 − N_{Ed} /(bhf_{ck} ), not less than 0.3: the coefficient of the enhanced moment.

[glossary-creep-ec2-5-8-8-3-4] Glossary: β (creep, EC2 5.8.8.3(4))
β (creep, EC2 5.8.8.3(4)): 0.35 + f_{ck} /200 − λ/150: how much creep raises the curvature of a column of slenderness λ.

[glossary-biaxial-bending] Glossary: biaxial bending
biaxial bending: Moments about both axes at once. Design each axis first; check together with Eq. 5.39 unless the screening says one axis dominates (EC2 5.8.9).

[glossary-creep-coefficient-t-0] Glossary: creep coefficient φ(∞,t_0 )
creep coefficient φ(∞,t_0 ): The final creep strain over the elastic strain, from EC2 Figure 3.1 or Annex B (RH, t_0 , h_0 , cement class).

[glossary-curvature-1-r] Glossary: curvature 1/r
curvature 1/r: K_r K_φ (1/r_0 ): the nominal curvature of the critical section.

[glossary-deflection-e-2] Glossary: deflection e_2
deflection e_2: (1/r)l_0 ²/c with c = 10: the second-order eccentricity at the critical section.

[glossary-effective-creep-ratio-ef] Glossary: effective creep ratio φ_{ef}
effective creep ratio φ_{ef}: φ(∞,t_0 ) × M_{0Eqp} /M_{0Ed} ; may be 0 if φ(∞,t_0 ) ≤ 2, λ ≤ 75 and M_{0Ed} /N_{Ed} ≥ h (EC2 5.8.4).

[glossary-enhanced-moment-m] Glossary: enhanced moment M′
enhanced moment M′: M_{Ed,z} + β(h′/b′)M_{Ed,y} (or the reverse): one moment about one axis that stands for both, used to estimate the bars (RDF §14, BS 8110).

[glossary-equivalent-first-order-moment-m-0e] Glossary: equivalent first-order moment M_{0e}
equivalent first-order moment M_{0e}: 0.6M_{02} + 0.4M_{01} ≥ 0.4M_{02} , opposite signs in double curvature: the first-order moment that goes with M_2 near mid-height (EC2 5.8.8.2(2)).

[glossary-exponent-a] Glossary: exponent a
exponent a: 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 at N_{Ed} /N_{Rd} = 0.1 / 0.7 / 1.0, interpolated: the power in Eq. 5.39.

[glossary-first-order-eccentricity-e-1] Glossary: first-order eccentricity e_1
first-order eccentricity e_1: The eccentricity of N_{Ed} before the column deflects: the analysed moment plus the imperfection, over N_{Ed} .

[glossary-imperfection-e-i] Glossary: imperfection e_i
imperfection e_i: l_0 /400 for a braced column; in biaxial bending taken about one axis at a time, the more unfavourable (EC2 5.2, 5.8.9(2)).

[glossary-interaction-check-eq-5-39] Glossary: interaction check, Eq. 5.39
interaction check, Eq. 5.39: (M_{Ed,z} /M_{Rd,z} )^a + (M_{Ed,y} /M_{Rd,y} )^a ≤ 1 for the bars provided (EC2 5.8.9(4)).

[glossary-k-r] Glossary: K_r
K_r: (n_u − n)/(n_u − n_{bal} ) ≤ 1: lowers the curvature of a heavily loaded column; iterated with the steel.

[glossary-k] Glossary: K_φ
K_φ: 1 + βφ_{ef} ≥ 1: raises the curvature for creep.

[glossary-minimum-eccentricity-e-0] Glossary: minimum eccentricity e_0
minimum eccentricity e_0: max(h/30, 20 mm): a floor on the design moment; in biaxial bending it goes with the imperfection.

[glossary-n-bal-n-u] Glossary: n_{bal} , n_u
n_{bal} , n_u: n_{bal} = 0.4, the axial load ratio at maximum moment resistance; n_u = 1 + ω, with ω = A_s f_{yd} /(A_c f_{cd} ).

[glossary-n-rd] Glossary: N_{Rd}
N_{Rd}: A_c f_{cd} + A_s f_{yd} : the axial resistance used for the exponent a.

[glossary-nominal-curvature-method] Glossary: nominal curvature method
nominal curvature method: EC2 5.8.8: M_2 from an assumed curvature at the critical section; the course method.

[glossary-nominal-stiffness-method] Glossary: nominal stiffness method
nominal stiffness method: EC2 5.8.7: the other simplified method, which reduces the stiffness and magnifies the first-order moment. Not used in this course.

[glossary-quasi-permanent-ratio-m-0eqp-m-0ed] Glossary: quasi-permanent ratio M_{0Eqp} /M_{0Ed}
quasi-permanent ratio M_{0Eqp} /M_{0Ed}: The share of the first-order moment that acts for a long time; 0.67 in the course unless the analysis gives it.

[glossary-relative-eccentricity] Glossary: relative eccentricity
relative eccentricity: e_y /h and e_z /b (h_{eq} , b_{eq} for other shapes): compared in the screening.

[glossary-screening-ec2-5-8-9-3] Glossary: screening (EC2 5.8.9(3))
screening (EC2 5.8.9(3)): Separate designs suffice if λ_y /λ_z and λ_z /λ_y ≤ 2 and one relative eccentricity ratio ≤ 0.2.

[glossary-second-order-moment-m-2] Glossary: second-order moment M_2
second-order moment M_2: N_{Ed} e_2 : the moment added by the deflection of a slender column.
